overview: A one-page U.S. Department of State list-of-papers sheet records a despatch from Taihoku and the Department’s response concerning a subsidy for Taiwan tea shipments. It notes that Bureau of Customs officials confirmed an October 26, 1939 letter from the Acting Commissioner of Customs stating that free-list imports were not liable to countervailing duties under section 303 of the Tariff Act of 1930; consequently, the consulate was instructed to take no action but to report subsequent developments.

people.name: Gerald Warner

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning subsidy for Taiwan tea shipments
subfiles.about: The sheet registers a Taihoku despatch and Departmental reply concerning the customs treatment of subsidized Taiwan tea shipments.
subfiles.summary: The Department records despatch no. 105 from Warner at Taihoku, dated May 2, and an apparent reply dated August 6. Customs officials confirmed an Acting Commissioner of Customs letter of October 26, 1939, which held that merchandise on the free list was not subject to countervailing duties under section 303 of the Tariff Act of 1930. No consular action was considered necessary, although the consulate was asked to keep the Department informed of further developments.

interest: This sheet concisely documents how U.S. officials applied American countervailing-duty law to subsidized Taiwanese tea during the period of Japanese colonial rule. It is useful for tracing the relationship between agricultural export subsidies, customs classification, and consular reporting, while its references to an otherwise absent despatch, reply, and Customs letter provide leads to related records elsewhere in the decimal file.
